text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain being in both knees and the right groin is very significant. Can you tell me if your right leg is turned outward and shortened compared to the left leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: That specific positioning—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is a classic presentation for a posterior hip dislocation. I am going to order an X-ray to confirm the diagnosis and check for any associated fractures. REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a posterior dislocation of the right hip without associated fractures. I need to rule out other injuries from the collision, so please confirm if you have any numbness or tingling in your right leg or foot. REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Spine_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The lumbar spine X-ray is normal, which is reassuring. Given the confirmed posterior hip dislocation, I need to ensure there is no nerve damage; can you move your right foot and toes normally without any weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the mechanism of injury and X-ray findings strongly support a posterior hip dislocation, and we have ruled out spinal involvement, I will proceed with the final assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior hip dislocation
